caption: The video captures a fixed close view of a small stream cascading through a narrow gap between two large rocks. The right boulder is coated in green moss, while translucent ice formations arch over and beside the water channel on the left and below. Red and orange autumn leaves lie scattered across the wet rock surfaces and frozen edges. A thin vertical sheet of falling water pours steadily through the gap into a dark, churning pool at the bottom center. The bright white streaks of the column and the foam spilling over the upper ice edge continually shift shape and position, marking an ongoing flow. The pool beneath shows moving bubbles and ripples whose pattern changes as the water strikes it. All solid elements, including the mossy rock, ice arches and protruding leaves, keep their positions while the water flows.
relations: Falling water and foam -> continually shift shape and position, marking ongoing flow.
Water striking the pool -> moving bubbles and ripples change pattern continuously.
Rocks, ice arches, and leaves -> remain fixed in position while water flows.
